task-intent.statement: Instantiate execute.json's c2 check (the verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py invocation) from COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json so later gates could trust it as a real, engine-run gate rather than a hand-authored one.

expected-behavior.statement: The template's c2 check command should resolve and run successfully from any worktree the spine was instantiated into, the same way every other engine-owned check does.

observed-behavior.statement: This run's execute.json had been instantiated with a relative form (`python scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py`) that can never resolve from a worktree, because `_installed_skills_root()` requires the script's own grandparent directory to be literally named `constellation-*` with true installed-skill siblings beside it (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/constellation-to-initial-issues`) -- a repo-source copy under a worktree's own `scripts/` never satisfies that. The canonical template already carries the correct absolute installed path (`py C:/Users/fredc/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py`); this spine's instantiation dropped that and substituted the relative repo-local form instead.

impact-cost.statement: A check that can never pass from any worktree is a check that can never fail meaningfully either -- it would have forced every future Commander instantiated from this same mis-substitution into either a bogus red or a hand-waived gate, silently weakening the one construct engine gates exist to provide. This is a template-instantiation defect, not a one-off, so it plausibly affects other Commanders' spines too.

workaround.statement: Repaired via `amend --op retext-check` (recorded at .agent-work/w3a-465/amend-c2-retext.json, authority Commander w3a-465-b) restoring the template's canonical absolute path, rather than hand-editing spine.json's JSON directly.

diagnosis.statement: `init_work_area.py --spine`'s placeholder substitution likely has a code path that can emit the relative form for this specific check even though the shipped COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json already carries the absolute form -- worth checking whether other already-instantiated Commander spines carry the same drift.

A cheap regression guard: an in-suite check that every checklist check.command referencing verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py (or any script mirroring an installed-skill script) uses the absolute installed path, not a repo-relative one, would catch this class at instantiation time instead of at whatever gate first tries to run it.

task-intent.statement: Query engine state with `current` against spine.json between mutating calls (claim, attest, advance), per the commander skill's 'ask the engine what to do next at every step' doctrine.

expected-behavior.statement: Since every mutating verb (claim/attest/attach/advance/start) on this spine requires `--session-id`, `current` -- a read-only status query on the same file -- would accept the same flag without complaint.

observed-behavior.statement: `python scripts/checklist_engine.py --file spine.json current --session-id <id>` exited 2 with 'unrecognized arguments: --session-id <id>' -- current's argparser does not define that flag at all, unlike every mutating verb. This is the same inconsistency an earlier session on this same run already flagged (2 failed reviewer calls, 1 Commander call) and it recurred verbatim this continuation session.

impact-cost.statement: One failed command this session; cheap in isolation, but it is a recurring, predictable trap for any agent that reflexively appends the flag it just used on the previous mutating call, and it has now cost calls across at least two separate Commander sessions on the same spine.

diagnosis.statement: current's argparse subparser was likely never updated when session-lease enforcement was added to the mutating verbs.

Either accept-and-ignore --session-id on current for symmetry, or have the error text on every mutating verb explicitly note that current is the one exception, so an agent copying the previous call's flags gets a directly actionable message instead of a bare argparse rejection.

task-intent.statement: Write a resume handoff instructing the successor how to apply the c2 check fix via the engine's amend verb.

expected-behavior.statement: The handoff assumed the engine's amend verb accepts an --op flag naming the operation directly on the command line (`amend --op retext-check`).

observed-behavior.statement: There is no --op flag; ops live inside the --delta file passed to amend. The implementer caught the mismatch and wrote the correct delta-file shape into the shipped template rather than parroting the Commander's invented syntax.

impact-cost.statement: A Commander inventing CLI syntax for a verb it is simultaneously establishing as authoritative in a shipped template is a credibility gap -- had the implementer trusted it instead of checking the real CLI contract, the amend would have failed at the exact point it mattered most.

workaround.statement: Implementer independently verified the actual amend CLI contract and used the delta-file form instead of the invented flag.

task-intent.statement: Write handoffs to the implementer and reviewer crews that name a consistent scratch/working-file location, so both crews use one convention and nothing lands untracked at the worktree root.

expected-behavior.statement: A named scratch directory in each handoff, matching the reviewer skill's own stated concern about orphan untracked scratch at the worktree root.

observed-behavior.statement: Neither handoff named one. The implementer improvised g1-implement/evidence/, the reviewer improvised its own separate reproduction tree, and both independently flagged the gap in their own reports.

impact-cost.statement: Two independent ad-hoc scratch conventions instead of one, and real risk of untracked scratch surviving past the reviewer's own gate at the worktree root -- a risk the reviewer skill separately warns about, so the omission has a concrete downstream consequence, not just a style preference.

workaround.statement: Both crews self-organized reasonable locations and flagged the gap explicitly rather than silently working around it or leaving scratch untracked.

task-intent.statement: Write a reviewer handoff criterion instructing verification of the c2 fix by inspecting the checklist's amendments array.

expected-behavior.statement: Every instruction in a reviewer handoff should be executable within doctrine -- i.e. reachable through an engine verb, never by reading checklist JSON directly.

observed-behavior.statement: No engine verb prints the amendments array, and reading the checklist JSON directly is a documented doctrine violation, so the criterion as written could not be honestly satisfied. The reviewer routed around it with an engine-verb-reachable equivalent and reported the mismatch instead of silently reading the JSON or silently skipping the criterion.

impact-cost.statement: A reviewer that had not caught this would have faced two silent failure modes -- violate doctrine via a direct JSON read, or skip verifying the criterion -- and either way the gate's assurance would have been hollow without anyone noticing.

workaround.statement: Reviewer substituted an engine-verb-reachable equivalent check and reported the handoff defect explicitly.

task-intent.statement: Satisfy the plan template's TDD red-phase gate with verifiable evidence, not merely a claim, since a command check cannot run the by-design-failing test without contaminating the gate itself.

expected-behavior.statement: Some recorded trace of the red run (e.g. a named file the failing-test output landed in) so a later reviewer or Commander can confirm the red actually happened and failed for the expected reason.

observed-behavior.statement: The template's red-phase check is check: null -- correctly, since a command check would literally run the test designed to fail -- but its postcondition is satisfied by bare self-attestation, with no artifact reference required at all.

impact-cost.statement: Nothing in the template currently forces a reviewer to be able to confirm the red actually ran and failed for the expected reason, versus a Commander merely asserting it did -- the gate's assurance rests on trust it does not itself require.

workaround.statement: This run's own TDD red was in fact captured in an evidence file under red/ even though the template did not require that -- the gap is in the template's default, not in what this run happened to do.

diagnosis.statement: Make the plan template's red-phase postcondition default to: attest the red AND name the file the failing-test output landed in, so the artifact reference becomes structural rather than incidental.
